Back to marketplace

Implementation and evidence · 18 October 2026

What works today.

Working local implementation. Sona connects Solana wallets, verifies Raydium CPMM Fee Keys, stores authenticated listings and builds an atomic exchange signed by both buyer and seller.

The settlement and full HTTP workflow have been executed against an isolated Solana validator. A separate read-only check validated an existing third-party Fee Key on mainnet. These are distinct results: no Sona mainnet sale, public production deployment or independent security audit is claimed.

The exchange

A seller lists a verified Fee Key at a fixed SOL price. A buyer requests the purchase. The seller signs a short-lived transaction, then the buyer reviews and signs the same transaction. It creates the buyer’s token account if needed, transfers exactly one Fee Key and pays the seller. All instruction effects succeed together or roll back together; transaction fees may still apply.

Listings and requests are hosted by Sona. Assets stay in the parties’ wallets until settlement. There is no Sona custody or new escrow program to deploy. Seller approval is required for each buyer, and an approval already released cannot be revoked by merely canceling a listing.

Current implementation

CapabilityImplementation and evidence
Wallet connectionWallet Standard and injected Phantom, Solflare and Backpack support. Public key, account changes, disconnect and exact-message signing are handled. Automated adapter tests do not substitute for an independently observed extension session.
Wallet balances and inventorySolana RPC reads and program-account validation. No seeded market, fictional balance or browser-local purchase state. The watchlist alone stays local.
Raydium eligibilityCPMM Burn & Earn Fee Keys only. Checks cover the current holder, NFT mint, canonical lock, pool, LP escrow and vault relationships. Live mainnet read evidence is linked below.
Listings and requestsSigned nonce authentication, shared SQLite persistence, exact lamport prices, listing expiry and authorized updates. Each sale requires both wallets.
Atomic settlementCanonical transaction checks in the browser and server; finalized confirmation before a completed sale is recorded. Local validator artifacts include actual instruction logs and before/after balances.
Public receiptsThe receipt endpoint exposes actual completed trades from this running service. Local test receipts are kept in separate evidence files and never inserted as marketplace trades.
Production statusLocal service only. No public source repository, independently verified mainnet sale or security review is recorded. The offline readiness gate remains closed for a production release.

  • Local HTTP-to-chain execution — authentication, persistent listing, both signatures, finalized receipt and restart persistence.
  • Mainnet read-only observation — an existing third-party Fee Key, with account hashes and a recorded slot. This is not a Sona sale, listing or customer.
  • Raydium source provenance — pinned official references, account layouts and eligibility limits.
  • Structured capability status and release declarations.

Scope and costs

The current integration transfers an entire CPMM Fee Key held by an ordinary signing wallet. Program-owned and multisig-held keys are not supported by this signing flow. It does not support CLMM positions, partial rights, LP redemption, fee claiming, new liquidity locks or confidential settlement. Public RPC can throttle; read failures are shown instead of fabricated holdings.

No paid API key is required for the local application. Listing does not require a deposit. A real purchase still costs Solana network fees and, when needed, buyer token-account rent. Public hosting and an independent review remain separate work.

The same source and evidence are available to every visitor. Recorded local execution, read-only mainnet verification and a completed mainnet marketplace sale are different claims. This page is not a score guarantee or security certification.
